target.learningOutcome: The learner can connect each Spring mapping annotation to its HTTP method, intended semantics, and a coherent order-resource example.
inScope: GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE semantics

claims.statement: @GetMapping, @PostMapping, @PutMapping, and @DeleteMapping are composed @RequestMapping annotations that select GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE respectively.
GET is safe and idempotent, PUT and DELETE are idempotent but not safe, and POST has no general idempotence guarantee under HTTP semantics.
A mapping annotation exposes a route but does not by itself make GET side-effect free or make a PUT or DELETE implementation idempotent.

examples.title: Exercise GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE mappings for one order resource

validation.command: Run gold.q2.MethodMappingsTest with Java 17, Spring Boot 3.3.1, and standalone MockMvc
validation.expected: The four HTTP methods reach their matching handlers; creation returns 201 and Location, deletion returns 204

notes: The comparison table keeps every method on one row and uses the same order resource as the code example.
